part1_strava.flow: OAuth 2.0 three-legged authorization-code flow only. swagger.json securityDefinitions: flow='accessCode', authorizationUrl=https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/authorize, tokenUrl=https://www.strava.com/api/v3/oauth/token. Web: GET https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize; mobile: GET https://www.strava.com/oauth/mobile/authorize (same code exchange afterwards).
part1_strava.pkce_or_public_client: NOT supported. Docs (checked 2026-09-13) list no PKCE/code_challenge parameters and no implicit or device flow; token exchange POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token requires client_id, client_secret, code, grant_type=authorization_code. Docs quote: 'The application must now call the POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token with its client ID and client secret to exchange the authorization code for a refresh token and short-lived access token' and 'The secret is used for authentication and should never be shared.' Community (Google group strava-api, 2020-08-29): 'there is no support for PKCE and your best bet would be to spin up a little server to host secrets and proxy requests to Strava.' No change found since.
part1_strava.consequence: A pure static site cannot complete the flow without exposing client_secret. Either (a) a tiny backend (Cloudflare Worker / Vercel function) performs the code-to-token exchange and refreshes, or (b) bring-your-own-app mode: each user creates their own Strava API application (capacity 1 = themselves) and pastes client_id + client_secret into the static app (localStorage). Option (b) is static-only and dodges the athlete cap, but onboarding friction is high and the getting-started page states 'A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app' (medium confidence: quoted from the fetched page summary).
part1_strava.token_lifetimes: Access tokens expire 6 h after creation; refresh via POST /oauth/token grant_type=refresh_token (returns a new access token if the current one expires in <= 1 h); every successful token call issues a new refresh token and the older one no longer works.

scopes_needed_for_pace.why: GET /athlete/activities and GET /activities/{id} require activity:read (activities visible to Everyone and Followers); add activity:read_all only if the user marks runs 'Only Me' (request it with an explanation; the user can untick it on the consent screen, so check the granted scope). profile:read_all is NOT needed (it only switches /athlete to the detailed representation). GET /athletes/{id}/stats documents no extra scope and 'Only includes data from activities set to Everyone visibility', so it under-reports for private runners.

endpoints.fields: recent_run_totals (last 4 weeks), ytd_run_totals, all_run_totals -> ActivityTotal {count, distance [m], moving_time [s], elapsed_time [s], elevation_gain [m], achievement_count}
endpoints.pace_signal: recent_run_totals.distance / recent_run_totals.moving_time = 4-week mean running speed [m/s] (mostly easy-run pace, about 0.65-0.75 VMA); 1 call, but visibility-filtered.

endpoints.params: before, after (epoch s), page (default 1), per_page (default 30; docs state no maximum; community practice 200, medium confidence)
endpoints.fields: SummaryActivity: sport_type (Run, TrailRun, VirtualRun), distance [m], moving_time [s], elapsed_time [s], average_speed [m/s], max_speed [m/s], workout_type (runs: 0 default, 1 race, 2 long run, 3 workout), manual, trainer, total_elevation_gain
endpoints.pace_signal: per-run average_speed; filter sport_type == Run, manual == false, distance >= 1000 m, last 90 days; median = easy pace, max of workout_type == 1 runs = race pace.

endpoints.fields: DetailedActivity = SummaryActivity + best_efforts: array[DetailedSegmentEffort] (documented in https://developers.strava.com/swagger/activity.json; legacy docs: 'array of best effort summaries', runs only, names such as 400m, 1/2 mile, 1k, 1 mile, 2 mile, 5k, 10k). Each effort: name, distance [m], elapsed_time [s], moving_time [s], start_date_local, pr_rank (1-3 or null).
endpoints.pace_signal: best 400m / 1k / 1 mile / 5k efforts across the last N runs. 1 read call per run: fetch only the ~10 most recent qualifying runs and cache.

rate_limits.overall: 200 requests per 15 min and 2,000 per day
rate_limits.read_non_upload: 100 requests per 15 min and 1,000 per day
rate_limits.exceed: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a JSON error
rate_limits.budget_math: One full profile refresh = 1 (/athlete/activities) + 1 (/athletes/{id}/stats) + <= 10 (/activities/{id}) = <= 12 read calls -> about 80 refreshes per day inside the 1,000/day read cap; cache the derived profile for 24 h.

athlete_capacity.unapproved_default: 1 connected athlete (single-player mode). Getting-started page: 'All new applications start in single-player mode. This is the default state where only your own Strava account can authenticate with the app.' Strava Community Manager (2024-07-12): 'all applications are created at an entry level athlete capacity of 1, aka single player mode.'
athlete_capacity.next_tier: Docs mention a 10-athlete tier; rate-limits page: 'Once your app reaches 10 connected athletes and you are ready to scale further, please submit your app for review'. Whether the 1 -> 10 step is automatic or itself needs the form is not stated unambiguously. Community: review takes about 7-10 business days; increases are 'not guaranteed' unless the app uses webhooks and throttling.
athlete_capacity.implication: Strava sync is effectively a personal/demo feature until the app passes Developer Program review. The pace model MUST work from manual inputs (tier, VMA, 5k time) first; Strava is an optional enhancer.

api_agreement_constraints: API Agreement update effective 2024-11-11: an athlete's Strava data may be displayed only to that athlete (fine here: pace is shown only to its owner; never push Strava-derived numbers into shared hack tables or leaderboards).
No use of API data to train AI/ML models; do not build a global pace prior from users' Strava data (use manual tier defaults instead).

Brand guidelines: OAuth must use a 'Connect with Strava' button linking to https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize; attribution 'Powered by Strava' or 'Compatible with Strava' logo, separate from and not more prominent than the app's own branding.
Support deauthorization (POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/deauthorize) and delete cached tokens plus derived data on disconnect.

recommended_backend.shape: Static site (GitHub Pages / Cloudflare Pages) + one Cloudflare Worker (or Vercel edge function) with 4 routes; client_secret lives only in the Worker secret store; the static bundle never contains it.
routes: GET /auth/callback?code=..&scope=.. -> POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token {client_id, client_secret, code, grant_type=authorization_code}; store {athlete_id, refresh_token, expires_at} in Workers KV keyed by a random opaque session id; set that id as an httpOnly SameSite cookie; 302 back to the static app. Verify the granted scope query parameter.

GET /api/pace -> (cookie -> KV) refresh the access token if expires_at - now < 3600 s; call /athlete/activities?after=<now-90d>&per_page=200, filter runs, then /activities/{id} for the <= 10 most recent qualifying runs; compute the profile; cache in KV for 24 h; return small JSON {vma_est_ms, v1k_best_ms, v5k_best_ms, v400_best_ms, recent_avg_ms, n_runs, confidence, updated_at}. Never return raw activities or GPS to the browser (keeps the display rule trivial and the payload tiny).
POST /api/disconnect -> POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/deauthorize with the access token; delete the KV entry; clear the cookie.
recommended_backend.derived_number: pace profile -> one fitness scalar VMA_est [m/s] plus a confidence label. Estimators (median of those available; weight best-effort estimators 2x): VMA = v_1k_best / 1.03 (a 1k best inside a normal run is a 3-5 min effort, about 100-105 % VMA); VMA = v_5k_best / 0.92 (5 km = 90-95 % VMA); VMA = race_avg_speed / 0.92 for workout_type == 1 runs of 5-10 km; VMA = recent_avg_speed / 0.70 (easy pace = 60-75 % VMA; low weight, high variance). Do not use 400 m best efforts for VMA (a within-run 400 m is rarely all-out) but keep v_400_best as an upper bound: v_open <= 0.95 * v_400_best. Hand VMA_est to the Part-2 model exactly like a manual VMA entry.
recommended_backend.cost: Cloudflare Workers free tier (100k requests/day) is ample; KV free tier stores tokens for thousands of users; roughly 150 lines of TypeScript.

free_flow_walking.source: Weidmann 1993 (literature synthesis; cited via Vanumu et al. 2017 review and Buchmueller & Weidmann 2006)

free_flow_walking.value: comfortable gait 1.27-1.46 m/s (women in their 70s .. men in their 40s); maximum walking 1.75-2.53 m/s (women 70s .. men 20s); n = 230
normal gait 0.94-1.43 m/s by age/sex stratum; n = 23,111
measured free-flow speed inside a German railway station 0.97-1.04 m/s, below Weidmann's 1.34 m/s
normal walking on flat 1.31-1.40 m/s; fast walking 1.71-1.84 m/s
design guides 1.4 m/s; Transport for London 1.33 m/s; preferred range 1.10-1.65 m/s

transit_planner_assumptions.value: 'average walking speed of 3 mph (5 km/h)' -> 400 m in 5 min; 'average walking speed of a younger adult is 4.0 ft/s (1.2 m/s)', 3.3 ft/s (1.0 m/s) when >= 20 % elderly; 3 s start-up and end clearance

SBB walk budgets imply (straight-line distance / budget): IWB -> Basel SBB 398 m / 8 min = 0.83 m/s; Margarethen 691 m / 11 min = 1.05 m/s; Markthalle 313 m / 8 min = 0.65 m/s; Central -> Zürich HB 282 m / 9 min = 0.52 m/s; Sihlquai/HB 313 m / 7 min = 0.74 m/s; Bahnhofquai/HB 99 m / 7 min = 0.24 m/s. The last shows the budget is a station-level constant, not a distance model.
transit_planner_assumptions.source: computed here (haversine) from transport.opendata.ch coordinates; Zürich HB 8503000 = 47.377847, 8.540502 fetched 2026-09-13
transit_planner_assumptions.confidence: high for the arithmetic; the station coordinate is a centroid, real platform paths are 1.2-1.6x longer

transit_planner_assumptions.value: SBB stores a per-stop transfer time (standard 2 min, Zürich HB 7 min) and only lets web users lengthen it (+50 % / +100 %), never shorten it
Net: SBB effectively budgets about 0.6-1.0 m/s door-to-platform including a fixed station buffer. A fit person walking at 1.4 m/s beats it by 30-50 %; running roughly halves it.

stairs_escalators.value: horizontal speed on stairs, young adults (Fujiyama & Tyler Group 2): normal ascent 0.56 / 0.63 / 0.76 m/s at 35 / 30.5 / 24.6 deg; normal descent 0.65 / 0.74 / 0.87; FAST ascent 0.91 / 0.97 / 1.16; FAST descent 0.92 / 1.08 / 1.18
Fruin 1971 field data (32 deg stairs): ascent 0.69 m/s young male, 0.51 young female; descent 0.69 / 0.51; over 50 y: 0.43 / 0.39 up
escalator nominal speed <= 0.75 m/s for <= 30 deg inclination, <= 0.50 m/s for 30-35 deg; 0.5-0.65 m/s typical

per 5 m level change (one station level; 30 deg stairs = 8.7 m horizontal, 10 m incline): stairs normal up 14 s, fast up 9 s, normal down 12 s, fast down 8 s; escalator standing 15-20 s (0.65-0.5 m/s); walking on the escalator 8-10 s; plus 2-3 s landing transitions each

tram_dwell_alighting.value: light-rail dwell regressions: constant 8.1-15.7 s (door cycle + operator), alighting 0.52-0.56 s per passenger, boarding 0.71-0.88 s per passenger, e.g. DT = 8.10 + 0.88*TONS + 0.22*LS; Koffman: DT = 3.0 + 0.75*TONS + 0.56*TOFFS + 0.035*PASS
alighting rates 0.4-2.6 passengers/s per door across systems
tram_dwell_alighting.source: TRB / Transport Reviews dwell-time literature (search summary)

tram_dwell_alighting.value: wheel-stop to feet on platform: 5-8 s standing at the door with a hand on the button; 10-20 s seated in a crowded low-floor tram with 5-15 people alighting ahead

running_physiology.value: VMA = VO2max / 3.5 (km/h, ml/kg/min); sustainable 4-8 min (fr.wikipedia) or 4-7 min (run-motion); beginners about 10 km/h, elite above 24 km/h (Kipchoge 24.3)
race fractions of VMA: 5 km 90-95 %; 10 km 85-92 % (typically 90 %); half 80-88 %; marathon about 80 % (Kipchoge 84 %); 100-400 m repetitions 100-115 % VMA

a 60-120 s effort (300 m) is physiologically feasible at 100-110 % VMA; the 60-75 % VMA effective figure for a station dash is an ENVIRONMENTAL outcome (crowd x luggage x doors/turns x stairs), not a physiological ceiling
load carriage: running speeds in the severe-intensity domain fall about 1 % per 1 % body mass carried (7-15 % BM backpacks); cost of transport +30 % at 15 % BM
running_physiology.confidence: high for the study; medium for transfer to a 5 kg commuter backpack (about 7 % BM -> about 7 % slower)

crowd_density.kladek_weidmann_formula: v(rho) = v0 * (1 - exp(-gamma * (1/rho - 1/rho_max))) with v0 = 1.34 m/s, gamma = 1.913 P/m^2, rho_max = 5.4 P/m^2 (parameter values from memory of Weidmann 1993; could not be re-fetched today -> medium confidence, verify before citing)
crowd_density.note: Walking multipliers about 0.97 / 0.79 / 0.45 at 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 P/m^2. Running through more than about 1 P/m^2 is not possible; hence the absolute caps below.

preset_tiers_m_s.basis: Fujiyama fast walk 1.71-1.84; Bohannon max walk 2.0-2.5
15 km/h = 95-100 % VMA; only meaningful in an empty station

fitness_inputs.vma_kmh: v_open = k_effort * VMA / 3.6 with k_effort = 0.75 (comfortable, default), 0.90 (committed), 1.00 (all-out; only for legs <= 90 s). Typical VMA: 10-12 km/h beginner, 13-16 recreational, 17-20 trained, above 20 competitive.
fitness_inputs.recent_5k_time_s: VMA_ms = (5000 / t5k) / f5k with f5k = 0.90 (t5k > 30 min), 0.92 (22-30 min), 0.95 (< 22 min); then treat as VMA.
fitness_inputs.strava: VMA_est from Part 1 (median of v1k/1.03, v5k/0.92, race_avg/0.92, recent_avg/0.70); confidence high if a 1k or 5k best effort from the last 90 days exists, low if only recent_avg.
fitness_inputs.tier_from_vma_for_display: map VMA_est to the nearest preset so the UI can always say, e.g., 'you are a run-tier commuter'.

formula.definition: sprint_time_s = t_alight + t_react + sum_over_segments(L_i / v_seg_i) + n_up * t_up + n_down * t_down + n_doors * t_door + t_board
formula.v_eff: v_eff = min( v_open * f_crowd * f_luggage , v_cap(crowd) )

f_crowd.basis: Weidmann FD multipliers 0.97 / 0.79 / 0.45 at 0.5 / 1 / 2 P/m^2 smoothed to four UI levels; derived, medium confidence

v_cap_m_s.basis: weaving through people caps running regardless of fitness; derived, low-medium confidence -> calibrate with logged attempts

f_luggage.basis: 1 % speed per 1 % body mass (PMID 29216289) for a 75 kg person; trolley value from experience, low confidence

level_change_s_per_5m.note: scale linearly with height / 5 m; multiply by 1 / f_crowd on stairs (queues at escalator entries in peak add 10-20 s, so prefer stairs in the model when both exist). Values = Fujiyama & Tyler speeds + 2-3 s transitions; medium confidence.

t_alight_s.basis: Lin & Wilson constants 3-15 s + 0.5 s per passenger ahead; derived

t_board_s.basis: TCQSM 3 s start-up + walking to the nearest open door of a 200-300 m train; derived, medium

slack_and_decision.door_close_lead_s: 20 s default (SBB long-distance doors close before departure; exact lead time NOT verified today -> uncertainty; make it a config constant)
slack_and_decision.margin_s: margin = max(45, 0.15 * sprint_time) + sigma_tram, where sigma_tram = 30 s if the tram has no realtime delay field in the API response, else 0

bands.basis: policy; the 45 s floor covers a red light on the Bahnhofbrücke or one missed door; 15 % covers pace variance (Weidmann SD/mean about 0.28 for walking speed; runners tighter)

worked_example_zurich_central.assumptions: path about 400 m Central -> Bahnhofbrücke -> Bahnhofquai entrance -> surface platform head (straight line 282 m; real path length to be measured by the geometry task), 0 level changes for platforms 3-18, commuter_peak crowd, backpack, tier run (v_open 3.3)
worked_example_zurich_central.margin: max(45, 32) = 45 s (+30 s if no realtime tram delay)
worked_example_zurich_central.budget_vs_sbb: about 4.3-4.8 min door-to-door vs SBB's 9 min walk budget from Central (and vs riding two more stops, about 3 min, plus 7 min from Bahnhofquai). Gain about 5-7 min, consistent with the commuter's 'saves up to 5 min'. Underground platforms 21-24 / 31-34 add 1-2 level changes (+12-24 s) and a longer path, eroding the gain, which matches his remark that it pays off on the surface platforms.

honest_display: Show the number the user can act on: 'be on platform X by hh:mm:ss' and the implied average speed as min/km AND as the nearest tier name ('jog pace with a backpack'), not a probability.
Show GO / RISKY / NO as colour plus text; in RISKY, state explicitly what breaks it ('a 30 s tram delay kills this').

Only recommend a hack when it is dominance-safe: the fallback if the sprint fails must be the connection SBB proposed anyway (same or later train from the same station). Never propose a hack whose failure strands the user (e.g. the last train).

Use realtime delay from transport.opendata.ch for both the tram (arrival at the alighting stop) and the train (departure); if the tram record has delay == null, widen the margin (sigma_tram) and label 'no live data'.

Let the user log the outcome (made it / missed / abandoned) with the measured sprint time; keep a per-hack empirical distribution and replace the model's sprint_time by the user's 80th-percentile logged time after 3 attempts.
Display the pace source and its confidence ('from Strava: 1k best 4:12 on 2026-08-30' vs 'from preset tier: assumed').
Never show Strava-derived pace numbers to anyone except the athlete (API Agreement 2024-11-11); community hack tables carry only tier-based defaults.

uncertainties: Whether Strava's 1 -> 10 athlete step is automatic or needs the Developer Program form; only the review beyond 10 is unambiguous.
per_page maximum for /athlete/activities is not stated in current docs (community: 200).
The statement 'A Strava subscription is a prerequisite for creating an app' came from the fetched getting-started page summary; verify on the page before relying on it.

best_efforts is present in the model file activity.json but absent from the rendered reference page; community reports it populated for runs only; whether Strava has moved best efforts behind subscription-only endpoints was not verifiable today.
Weidmann/Kladek FD parameters (1.34, 1.913, 5.4) are from memory; the review fetched today confirms 1.34 m/s but not gamma / rho_max.
SBB door-closing lead time before scheduled departure (assumed 20 s) not verified.

SBB per-stop transfer times (2 min standard, 7 min Zürich HB) come from a community thread summary, not an official document; HRDF/METABHF or GTFS transfers.txt on opentransportdata.swiss would give official values.
All crowd multipliers/caps and level-change costs are derived estimates (medium/low confidence) and need calibration from logged attempts.
Path lengths (Central -> platform, IWB -> south entrance -> platform) were not measured in this task; the worked example assumes 400 m.
